Bunnie Xo revealed the physical toll heartbreak has taken on her as she navigates her div...
articles.body_text:
Jelly Roll tells Fox News Digital what it means to him to celebrate the 60th Academy of Country Music Awards.

Bunnie Xo revealed the physical toll heartbreak has taken on her as she navigates her divorce from Jelly Roll.

"There were moments where my team had to pick me up off the floor and get me IVs because I wasn't eating," Bunnie said during an appearance on "Open Book with Jenna Bush Hager."

"I was eating baby food to get by, you know," she admitted. "I lost 20 pounds because of heartbreak.'"

JELLY ROLL FILES FOR DIVORCE FROM WIFE BUNNIE XO AFTER ALMOST A DECADE OF MARRIAGE

Bunnie Xo detailed previous strains in her relationship with Jelly Roll after news broke about their divorce. (Christopher Polk)

Jelly Roll filed for divorce from Bunnie Xo on May 18, but the "Son of a Sinner" singer listed the date of separation as May 9. The two first met in 2015 after the former sex worker met the rising star at a concert in Las Vegas, and they eloped a year later.

Bunnie Xo and Jelly Roll were married nearly 10 years before their divorce was finalized in July.

Shortly after announcing the divorce, Bunnie Xo used her podcast to share the intimate details of the split. She later deleted it from YouTube.

BUNNIE XO SAYS SHE FUNDED JELLY ROLL'S EARLY CAREER BY 'TURNING TRICKS' WHILE REFLECTING ON DIVORCE

Bunnie Xo revealed she's lost 20 pounds in the aftermath of her divorce from Jelly Roll. (Taylor Hill/Getty Images)

"Oh, everybody loves to watch a train wreck. So, I mean, yeah, I was not going to participate in that circus," she told Hager. "I am my own person. I stand on my own two feet, even alongside my ex-husband."

"I was still my own entity and had my own brand aside from him," she added. "So, yeah, I don't see why I couldn't continue to stand on my own two feet and not have to dwell in that space of emotion."

As Bunnie picks up the pieces after the end of her nearly decade-long marriage, she said she’s entered a new chapter focused on putting herself first – without feeling guilty about it.

GET ENTERTAINMENT SCOOP DELIVERED RIGHT TO YOUR EMAIL BY CLICKING HERE

Bunnie Xo is seen at the 60th Academy of Country Music Awards on May 8, 2025. (Christopher Polk/Penske Media via Getty Images)

"It's just pouring back into yourself," she explained. "It's being selfish. It's OK to be selfish. We as women feel like we need permission to be selfish, and we don't. Tell your kids to go to bed and eat the freaking brownies without them, you know? Even if it's something as small as that, we deserve to be selfish."

"We deserve to have our own time, and we deserve to pour into each other," Bunnie added. "I'm having so much fun."

LIKE WHAT YOU'RE READING? CLICK HERE FOR MORE ENTERTAINMENT NEWS

Bunnie Xo and Jelly Roll were married for nearly 10 years. (Weiss Eubanks/NBCUniversal via Getty Images)

And while Bunnie has been enjoying her newfound freedom, she insists her post-divorce adventures haven’t been nearly as scandalous as some might assume from what they see online.

"I mean, it's been – you know, it's so funny – people probably think I'm out here doing, like, ho activities, and I'm not," she claimed. "I swear to God. Literally, we're at home playing – what's it called? – Cards Against Humanity … We're swimming, we're working out. You guys see only what I put on social media."

PUT YOUR ENTERTAINMENT KNOWLEDGE TO THE TEST AND SEE HOW YOU SCORE

Bunnie Xo revealed how she's been spending her time after her divorce from Jelly Roll. (Dia Dipasupil/Getty Images)

In early July, Bunnie was spotted with a new, younger man. In video obtain by TMZ, Bunnie Xo could be seen kissing 24-year-old reality star Dylan Wolf in Nashville at Jelly Roll's bar.

She clarified that not everyone she's seen out with is a romantic partner.

"I'm like, 'Can your girl have some fun?' I'm going – you guys are going to see me with multiple men, maybe even a couple women," Bunnie joked. "You never know. Maybe even a freaking camel."

articles.title: Christie Brinkley shares how she keeps her three adult children coming home
articles.excerpt:
Christie Brinkley, star of "American Summer," explains why losing both parents made family time more precious and shares how she keeps her children close.

Christie Brinkley never really had to face a...
articles.body_text:
Christie Brinkley, star of "American Summer," explains why losing both parents made family time more precious and shares how she keeps her children close.

Christie Brinkley never really had to face an empty nest.

The actress and supermodel stars opposite Steve Guttenberg in "American Summer," a feel-good tribute to simpler times and family connections. The 72-year-old told Fox News Digital that those themes aren't just on-screen — they're values she's embraced in her own life, creating a home her three adult children can still return to.

The movie, which hit theaters Sept. 4, follows Guttenberg's character as he looks back on a formative childhood summer filled with baseball, first love and the disappearance of his U.S. Army father overseas.

CHRISTIE BRINKLEY HAS FANS MISTAKING SUPERMODEL FOR DAUGHTER IN NEW PHOTOS

Christie Brinkley's new movie, "American Summer, hit theaters on Sept. 4, 2026. (Blue Harbor Entertainment)

"I have always been all about family, so I have built my life in a way that my kids ... I want them independent," Brinkley said. "I want them out there living, doing whatever, but they always tend to come home on weekends, holidays. We all really are big on being together, and I love that."

Christie Brinkley and daughters Sailor Lee Brinkley-Cook and Alexa Ray Joel arrive at the Sports Illustrated Swimsuit 2017 launch event at Center415 Event Space in New York City on Feb. 16, 2017. (GC Images)

"It's funny because a lot of moms on Instagram will ask me, 'How do you get your kids to come home so often? Mine are off and about,'" the Sports Illustrated Swimsuit cover girl shared. "And I think it's just to always let them know they're always welcome back. They can bring their friends, that kind of thing."

Christie Brinkley's children — Alexa Ray Joel, Jack Paris Brinkley-Cook and Sailor Brinkley-Cook — remain a central part of her life. (Getty Images)

The supermodel is often photographed alongside her three grown children — Alexa Ray Joel, 40, Jack Paris Brinkley-Cook, 31, and Sailor Brinkley-Cook, 28 — whether they're walking red carpets or stepping out in coordinated looks. Brinkley said their close bond didn't happen by accident but was rooted in the example set by her own parents.

WATCH: CHRISTIE BRINKLEY SHARES SECRET TO KEEPING HER FAMILY CLOSE

After losing both of her parents less than two months apart in 2012, Brinkley said she no longer takes family time for granted. Her father, Don Brinkley, died July 14, followed by her mother, Marge Brinkley, on Sept. 9.

"I have always cherished my family time," Brinkley said. "And I think once you lose both of your parents, it becomes more precious because you know that there is a finite time to it. And right now, our family's smaller because I don't have my mom and dad."

Alexa Ray Joel and Christie Brinkley appear onstage at the Big Apple Circus in New York City on Feb. 1, 2020. (Getty Images for Big Apple Circus)

Brinkley became visibly emotional before saying, "I always get choked up whenever I talk about them."

Christie Brinkley's parents attend a pageant in Hawaii, date unknown. (Corbis via Getty Images)

Guttenberg is no stranger to Brinkley's heartbreak. He became a caregiver for his father, Stanley Guttenberg, after he developed kidney failure, eventually training to help administer dialysis at home.

"I remember you telling me about your mom and dad, Christie, that you had a little house on your property, and they lived near you, right?" Guttenberg said. "Isn't that wonderful? How lucky you were and are to have them right there. It's priceless, right? ... The greatest thing in the world."

Family came first for Steve Guttenberg, who paused his acting career to help care for his father, Stanley Guttenberg. (Blue Harbor Entertainment)

"The best," Brinkley replied. "My parents were always, always so ready to be there for me. Good times, bad times, they were always there, and they always made an effort to be a family. And I think it's so important, and it has given me my happiest moments."

GET ENTERTAINMENT SCOOP DELIVERED RIGHT TO YOUR EMAIL BY CLICKING HERE

"American Summer" is described as a homage to families in small-town America. (Blue Harbor Entertainment)

Family continues to be an essential part of Brinkley's life. She shared that Alexa Ray was preparing for a concert that night, while Jack planned to attend the premiere of "American Summer" alongside her.

For Brinkley, the movie's message extends beyond the screen. She believes audiences are craving stories that celebrate family.

Christie Brinkley and Sailor Brinkley Cook attend the Solving Kids Cancer Annual Hamptons Luncheon at Tutto II Giorno in Southampton, N.Y., on Aug. 4, 2025. (Sonia Moskowitz/Getty Images)

"... People want to put down their phone and speak to another human face to face," she said. "... This [story] takes us back before there were cell phones. And I think that we're going to find people now putting down their cell phones more often and just connecting with loved ones. And that human connection, nothing can replace it. I find that whenever I light a little bonfire in the backyard or at the beach, I always say, 'This is it. This is free. This is simple. And you know what? This is as good as it gets.'"

Steve Guttenberg and Christie Brinkley are seen here in a scene from "American Summer." (Blue Harbor Entertainment)

"Just to be able to sit there by the crackling of the fire, the moon coming up, the stars sparkling, the birds chirping, the crickets coming on, the fireflies lighting — that's it," she continued. "That's the best. Slowing down the speed of life, human connections ... I think those are things that we all want to feel again and again."

"It's better than any Ferrari," Guttenberg said.

Christie Brinkley poses with son Jack at the opening night arrivals for Michael Moore's "The Terms of My Surrender" on Broadway at the Belasco Theatre in New York City on Aug. 10, 2017. (Bruce Glikas/FilmMagic)

Brinkley's love of simple pleasures doesn't stop with family gatherings. She's also an avid birdwatcher — a hobby she believes is making a comeback as more people look to unplug.

LIKE WHAT YOU'RE READING? CLICK HERE FOR MORE ENTERTAINMENT NEWS

Christie Brinkley attends Best Friends Animal Society's "The Spirit of the Sanctuary" benefit on Aug. 24, 2026, at Jill Rappaport's Last Buck Ranch in Water Mill, New York. (Getty Images)

"I've always been a birdwatcher," she said. "On my Instagram, I have a bird feeder, and if you go back, you'll see lots and lots of pictures of the birds at my bird feeder. And I was just reading that birdwatching is back in full force for young people, too. People want to connect with nature. They want to get in nature, and it's all part of just that slowing down."

WATCH: CHRISTIE BRINKLEY REVEALS THE LONGTIME HOBBY HELPING HER SLOW DOWN

PUT YOUR ENTERTAINMENT KNOWLEDGE TO THE TEST AND SEE HOW YOU SCORE

Alexa Ray Joel and Christie Brinkley attend the SASF Sweet 16th Unconditional Love Gala on July 19, 2025, in Bridgehampton, N.Y. (Sonia Moskowitz/Getty Images)

And after raising three children, Brinkley believes that slowing down and making time for family helps keep loved ones coming back home.

Stephanie Nolasco is an Entertainment Reporter for Fox News Digital.

articles.title: Prince William to attend King Harald's funeral in Norway
articles.excerpt:
Harald, the popular King of Norway, is to be buried in Oslo next week

The Prince of Wales will attend the funeral of King Harald V of Norway on Wednesday in Oslo, Buckingham Palace has announced.

Al...
articles.body_text:
Harald, the popular King of Norway, is to be buried in Oslo next week

The Prince of Wales will attend the funeral of King Harald V of Norway on Wednesday in Oslo, Buckingham Palace has announced.

Also going to the funeral, in a personal capacity, is Princess Anne, who is godmother to Norway's new monarch, King Haakon VIII.

The late King Harald, a popular, modernising figure who had been on the Norwegian throne for 35 years, died last month at the age of 89.

Royal sources say Prince William's attendance, representing his father King Charles, follows the convention that the monarch does not usually go to the funeral of another head of state.

Large crowds are expected for the farewell to King Harald on 9 September, with a funeral procession to be followed by a service at Oslo Cathedral.

Thousands have queued to pay their respects to the late king, during his lying in state in the chapel of the Royal Palace in the Norwegian capital.

At the funeral, alongside Prince William, will be the widowed Queen Sonja, members of the Norwegian royal family including new King Haakon VIII, and other European royals.

The service will be followed by a private burial in Norway's royal mausoleum in the Akershus Fortress.

People have queued to pay their respects to King Harald at the Royal Palace Chapel

Among the tributes to King Harald was an emotional televised speech by his son King Haakon, who said: "Thank you for being such a good dad."

Harald had been seen as a down to earth "people's king" who had helped to modernise the monarchy, broken with tradition by marrying a commoner and served as a unifying figure.

His son said he represented the values of a "society built on law and justice, where everyone is of equal value".

King Charles's message praised his cousin King Harald for serving his people with "unwavering dedication, guiding Norway through times of great change with warmth and humility".

Prince William and Kate with the then-Crown Prince Haakon and his wife Mette-Marit during a visit to Oslo in 2018

King Haakon assumes his role at a difficult time, with the Norwegian royal family facing scandals this year.

His wife, Queen Mette-Marit, came under scrutiny when it was revealed she had maintained a three-year friendship with the sex offender Jeffrey Epstein, for which she publicly apologised.

Her son from a previous relationship, Marius Borg Høiby, was convicted in June of rape and other offences and sentenced to four years in prison. He is appealing.

While Prince William will be in Norway, King Charles has returned to Scotland, after meeting President Macron of France at the Bayeux Tapestry exhibition in London this week.

The King will be hosting Andy Burnham at Balmoral this weekend, in the traditional annual visit of the prime minister to stay with the monarch.

articles.title: North Carolina Dem Senate candidate added former Bloods gang member to criminal justice task force: report
articles.excerpt:
Fox News Flash top headlines are here. Check out what's clicking on FoxNews.com.

Roy Cooper, the former Democrat governor of North Carolina now running for Senate, added an ex-member of the notorious...
articles.body_text:
Fox News Flash top headlines are here. Check out what's clicking on FoxNews.com.

Roy Cooper, the former Democrat governor of North Carolina now running for Senate, added an ex-member of the notorious Bloods gang to a "Racial Equity in Criminal Justice" task force in 2020.

In the wake of George Floyd's 2020 death, Cooper created the task force via executive order, The Washington Free Beacon reported.

Cooper, who tapped then state attorney general turned current Gov. Josh Stein to lead the task force, stocked the panel with a mix of state officials and community activists, including Kerwin Pittman, who was convicted in 2007 of conspiracy to commit murder, serving 14 years in prison for the crime, according to records obtained by the Free Beacon.

Pittman was also identified as a "ranking member of the Bloods" by prosecutors during a murder trial for Bloods member Michael Contrez Jones.

SIX-FIGURE PRIVATE SECURITY BILL FOR TOP DEM SENATE HOPEFUL FUELS GOP HYPOCRISY CLAIMS

Emancipate NC's Kerwin Pittman speaks with reporters during a news conference, Aug. 3, 2023, outside the Gaston County Courthouse in Gastonia, N.C. (Reuters, File)

Pittman was convicted in connection to the 2006 drive-by-shooting of 19-year-old Jamel Amiens Jeffreys, the Free Beacon reported.

Pittman defended his involvement in the task force and argued his past actions were the result of poor judgment as a teenager.

"I was asked to contribute to conversations about criminal justice reform because of both my lived experience and the work I was doing in communities," Pittman told the Free Beacon. "I have never hidden my past. The gang involvement and criminal conduct you reference occurred when I was a teenager and young man, at or before the age of 19. I am now 39 years old."

ONE YEAR AFTER IRYNA ZARUTSKA MURDER, VIOLENT CRIMES FUEL NORTH CAROLINA PUBLIC SAFETY DEBATE

North Carolina Democratic Senate candidate former Gov. Roy Cooper, right, shares a moment with his wife, Kristin Cooper, left, as he speaks at a primary election night watch in Raleigh, N.C. (Matt Ramey/AP Photo, File)

"I made decisions as a young person that had serious consequences, including spending more than a decade incarcerated," he added.

Pittman, according to his LinkedIn profile, worked at the time of the task force's creation for Emancipate NC, an organization which, as the Free Beacon reported, has often called for the abolition of police, writing that "maintaining white supremacy has always been the goal of policing," in a 2023 company blog post.

Cooper, who is running for Senate against former Republican National Committee Chairman Michael Whatley, referenced his opponent's record when asked to comment on the Free Beacon story.

DEM SENATE HOPEFUL PIVOTS ON DATA CENTERS AS RISING POWER COSTS COLLIDE WITH CAMPAIGN

North Carolina Democratic Senate candidate former Gov. Roy Cooper speaks at a primary election night watch party March 3 in Raleigh, N.C. (Matt Ramey/AP Photo, File)

"While Roy spent his career putting rapists and violent criminals behind bars and signing tough on crime laws as governor, Michael Whatley spent his appointing a convicted child sex predator who served six years in prison and spent over a decade as a registered sex offender to a top role within the North Carolina Republican Party that gave him access to events with children," the Cooper campaign told Fox News Digital in a statement.

Pittman and the Whatley campaign did not immediately respond to Fox News Digital’s request for comment.

articles.title: Your daily coffee habit could be taking a toll on your bones, new study suggests
articles.excerpt: Dr. Alexa Fiffick, a board-certified family medicine physician and founder of Concierge Medicine of Westlake in Cleveland, Ohio, speaks about a new study linking hormone replacement therapy to lower d...
articles.body_text:
Dr. Alexa Fiffick, a board-certified family medicine physician and founder of Concierge Medicine of Westlake in Cleveland, Ohio, speaks about a new study linking hormone replacement therapy to lower dementia risk.

If you’re a woman who regularly reaches for coffee throughout the day, you may want to think twice about that next cup — or consider switching to tea.

Researchers at Flinders University reported in a study published in the journal Nutrients that high coffee consumption may be associated with lower bone mineral density (BMD) in older, postmenopausal women.

COFFEE MAY HAVE POWERFUL EFFECT ON LIVER HEALTH, MAJOR STUDY SUGGESTS

The scientists analyzed coffee and tea consumption among 9,704 women age 65 and older over a 10-year period. During that time, they also measured participants’ BMD at the femoral neck and hip — areas where osteoporosis-related fractures commonly occur.

The researchers found that drinking tea was associated with higher total hip BMD, while drinking more than five cups of coffee per day was associated with lower BMD.

Drinking more than five cups of coffee per day was associated with lower bone mineral density in older women, according to the study. (iStock)

Moderate coffee consumption — about two to three cups a day — was not associated with negative effects on bone health.

The study also identified differences based on other health and lifestyle factors. Coffee consumption was associated with lower femoral neck BMD among women with higher alcohol intake, while the positive association between tea and bone density was more pronounced among women with obesity.

The researchers wrote that osteoporosis, which is characterized by low BMD, "is a major global public health concern affecting individuals across all ages, genders and ethnicities."

About one in three women and one in five men age 50 and older worldwide experience osteoporosis-related fractures, according to the study.

CLICK HERE TO SIGN UP FOR OUR LIFESTYLE NEWSLETTER

Women face a particularly high risk because they generally have lower bone mass and experience accelerated bone loss after menopause.

In the U.S., the number of adults age 50 and older with low BMD in the hip or spine is projected to increase by 17.2 million by 2030, adding to the healthcare costs and long-term disability associated with osteoporosis-related fractures, the researchers noted.

Coffee lovers may not need to give up their daily brew, researchers said, but consuming more than five cups per day could be linked to lower bone density. (iStock)

The scientists wrote that they studied the relationship between coffee and tea and bone health because dietary factors play a "crucial role in the prevention of noncommunicable disease and may influence bone health," and these are two of the most widely consumed beverages globally.

TEST YOURSELF WITH OUR LATEST LIFESTYLE QUIZ

Study co-author Ryan Liu told ScienceDaily that "compounds called catechins, abundant in tea, may promote bone formation and slow bone breakdown."

"Coffee’s caffeine content, by contrast, has been shown in laboratory studies to interfere with calcium absorption and bone metabolism, though these effects are small and can be offset by adding milk," Liu said.

Older women who drank tea had higher bone density in the hip than those who did not, according to a study. (iStock)

"Our results don't mean you need to give up coffee or start drinking tea by the gallon," Liu added. "But they do suggest that moderate tea consumption could be one simple way to support bone health, and that very high coffee intake might not be ideal, especially for women who drink alcohol."

Symptoms of osteoporosis and early bone loss include back pain, loss of height over time and stooped posture, according to the Mayo Clinic.

Steps that can help prevent bone loss and support bone health include eating calcium-rich foods, such as dairy products, leafy greens and canned fish with bones; getting adequate vitamin D, which helps the body absorb calcium; and exercising regularly, particularly through weight-bearing and strength-training exercises.

Balance exercises can also help reduce the risk of falls and fractures.

Teresa Mull is a freelance writer with the Lifestyle team at Fox News Digital.

articles.title: Father of Patrick Mahomes asks court to attend son's games amid probation for driving while intoxicated
articles.excerpt:
Patrick Mahomes Sr., who is on probation after pleading guilty to driving while intoxicated, filed a motion to try to see his son, Patrick Mahomes, play this season.

Mahomes Sr. filed the motion Frid...
articles.body_text:
Patrick Mahomes Sr., who is on probation after pleading guilty to driving while intoxicated, filed a motion to try to see his son, Patrick Mahomes, play this season.

Mahomes Sr. filed the motion Friday in the 7th District Court in Tyler, Texas, according to FOX10. He requested permission to leave the state for seven of his son’s games in Kansas City, Missouri; Las Vegas, Nevada; and Cincinnati, Ohio, according to FOX10.

In the motion, Mahomes Sr. acknowledges that to leave the state, he must submit to urinalysis testing both before and after he travels and notify a supervising officer each time he departs the state.

CLICK HERE FOR MORE OUTKICK SPORTS COVERAGE

Pat Mahomes, father of Kansas City Chiefs quarterback Patrick Mahomes, looks on after the Chiefs defeated the Tennessee Titans 35-24 in the AFC Championship Game at Arrowhead Stadium on Jan. 19, 2020, in Kansas City, Mo. (David Eulitt/Getty Images)

Mahomes Sr. pleaded guilty to driving while intoxicated in 2024 and was sentenced to five years of probation. He was arrested in February 2026 on charges of violating the terms of his probation after drinking alcohol, according to Smith County District Attorney Jacob Putman.

The violation extended his probation by another two years.

The motion Mahomes Sr. filed noted that he completed 16 weeks of outpatient treatment and 160 hours of community service. The motion also states that Mahomes Sr. has complied with all current probation conditions and is monitored by an ankle monitor, both of which can be verified by a Smith County community supervision officer.

ZERO BS. JUST DAKICH. TAKE THE DON'T @ ME PODCAST ON THE ROAD. DOWNLOAD NOW!

Pat Mahomes, father of Patrick Mahomes II, quarterback for the Kansas City Chiefs, watched the team warmup prior to the game against the San Francisco 49ers at Arrowhead Stadium on Sept. 23, 2018 in Kansas City, Missouri. (David Eulitt/Getty Images)

OutKick reached out to Mahomes Sr.'s attorney and Mahomes' representatives for comment, but did not immediately get a response.

The Chiefs open the season against the Denver Broncos on Monday Night Football in Week 1 and while it’s not confirmed Mahomes will start, he appears on track to be on the field.

The two-time MVP underwent surgery in December to repair torn ligaments in his knee, yet he has still managed to work with the first team throughout training camp. He did not play in any preseason games.

Patrick Mahomes of the Kansas City Chiefs celebrates with his father Pat Mahomes after the AFC Championship NFL football game at M&T Bank Stadium on January 28, 2024 in Baltimore, Maryland. (Kara Durrette/Getty Images)

"He's going to keep practicing just like he's been doing," Chiefs coach Andy Reid told reporters Wednesday. "These are more like practice here, a lot of one-versus-one play these next couple of days. That's a good thing."

Ryan Canfield is a digital production assistant for Fox News Digital.

articles.title: Fighter jet crashes at air show, killing 2 pilots with thousands of spectators watching
articles.excerpt:
A Greek air force fighter jet crashed and burst into flames during an air show with thousands of spectators. (Credit: @sovva1_1 via Storyful and REUTERS).

A day at the air show turned fatal on Saturd...
articles.body_text:
A Greek air force fighter jet crashed and burst into flames during an air show with thousands of spectators. (Credit: @sovva1_1 via Storyful and REUTERS).

A day at the air show turned fatal on Saturday when a Greek air force jet crashed north of Athens as thousands of spectators watched.

Both pilots were killed in the crash at Tanagra air force base but no civilians were hurt.

The twin-seat Phantom F4 jet flew into the ground during a low-altitude maneuver just meters above the ground.

EIGHT BELIEVED DEAD AFTER B-52 CRASHES SHORTLY AFTER TAKEOFF FROM EDWARDS AIR FORCE BASE

Spectators watch as smoke rises after a Hellenic Air Force F-4 Phantom fighter jet crashed during the Athens Flying Week airshow at Tanagra Air Force Base, north of Athens, Greece, on Saturday. (AP Photo/Kallista Allaway)

"The sense of grief is widespread, and our thoughts are with the families of the two pilots we lost," Prime Minister Kyriakos Mitsotakis said. "It is a reminder of the daily danger faced by Greece’s aviators, who remain on constant standby to protect Greece's skies."

The jet burst into flames on impact, sending up a large plume of black smoke, prompting 11 water-dropping planes and helicopters to assist 85 firefighters in extinguishing the blaze.

11 SKYDIVERS, ONE PILOT KILLED IN MISSOURI PLANE CRASH NEAR AIRPORT

Video of the crash showed a second ball of fire nearby as the plane broke apart.

The bodies of the pilots were eventually recovered.

Smoke rises after a Hellenic Air Force F-4 Phantom fighter jet crashed during the Athens Flying Week airshow at Tanagra Air Force Base, north of Athens, Greece, on Saturday. (AP Photo/undefined)

"We were all stunned. It hadn't been airborne for more than three minutes," an eyewitness told ERT, Greece’s state-owned broadcaster.

The crash happened during the country’s annual Athens Flying Week.

The organizers canceled the rest of the events following the incident and the area was evacuated.

Two pilots were killed in the crash. (via REUTERS)

"It is with deep sadness that I learned of the death of the two officers of the Hellenic Air Force, who lost their lives in the tragic accident that occurred during the air show at Tanagra Air Base," Cyprus' Defense Minister Vasilis Palmas said, adding that he had called Nikos Dendias, Greece’s Minister of National Defense.

AIR FORCE IDENTIFIES 8 CREW MEMBERS KILLED IN B-52 STRATOFORTRESS CRASH AT EDWARDS AIR FORCE BASE

The air force has declared three days of mourning in the country.

In May, two jets collided during an air show in Idaho, but the pilots were able to safely eject.

The Associated Press and Reuters contributed to this report.

Brie Stimson is a Los Angeles-based entertainment and breaking news writer for Fox News Digital.

It has been dormant for decades, but the row between Argentina and the United Kingdom over the Falkland Islands ...
articles.body_text:
President Javier Milei says sovereignty over the islands remains a national objective.

It has been dormant for decades, but the row between Argentina and the United Kingdom over the Falkland Islands has been revived.

It started with a joint British-Israeli oil exploration project off the archipelago’s north coast, to which Buenos Aires vehemently objected.

President Javier Milei has now threatened to sanction companies operating there.

His push to reclaim the islands was bolstered by United States President Donald Trump’s comment that he may reconsider Washington’s position on the territory.

Britain and Argentina went to war over the islands more than four decades ago.

Could the dispute escalate into another armed confrontation?

articles.title: Everton vs Manchester United: Premier League – prediction, teams, lineups
articles.excerpt:
Who: Everton vs Manchester United
What: English Premier League
Where: Hill Dickinson Stadium in Liverpool, United Kingdom
When: Sunday, August 6, at 2pm (13:00 GMT).
How to follow: Al Jazeera Sport wi...
articles.body_text:
Who: Everton vs Manchester United
What: English Premier League
Where: Hill Dickinson Stadium in Liverpool, United Kingdom
When: Sunday, August 6, at 2pm (13:00 GMT).
How to follow: Al Jazeera Sport will have all the build-up from 10:00 GMT ahead of our live coverage.

Manchester United manager Michael Carrick said he is delighted with the additions to his squad despite being outspent by Premier League rivals in the transfer window and short on depth in some areas.

United put their efforts into rebuilding Carrick’s midfield, with Casemiro’s exit and a serious injury to Manuel Ugarte offset by the acquisitions of Andrey Santos, Youri Tielemans and Carlos Baleba for a combined 155 million pounds ($210m).

The Red Devils’ fiercest rivals spent almost that budget on a single player as Manchester City broke the British transfer record for Enzo Fernandez, while Liverpool splashed up to 123 million pounds ($166m) on French winger Bradley Barcola.

Despite returning to the Champions League for the first time in three seasons, Carrick hinted at having to work within financial restrictions.

“We went into the window wanting to come out stronger from the group that we had last season. We’ve definitely added to that,” Carrick told a pre-match media conference ahead of Sunday’s trip to Everton.

“I think we’ve done a lot of good work in that respect and the situation is what it is in terms of finances and what we can work with and what we’re trying to get the most of.

“Certainly, the players that we’ve brought into the group I’m absolutely delighted with and I think we’ve done some really good business there.”

United look particularly short in defence with the injury-prone Luke Shaw their only senior option at left-back.

“What squad ever is the perfect squad? You’ve always got to find ways of adapting,” Carrick added.

“When you’re building and trying to push to go through a period where we’re trying to get to the top – that’s the ultimate goal – you’ve got to make steps.”

Joshua Zirkzee was among those expected to leave Old Trafford to boost the funds available to Carrick.

Despite interest from Fiorentina and Juventus and a deadline-day approach from Everton, the Netherlands international remains at United, despite limited game time over the past two seasons.

“He wants to play more than he has done and that’s the good competition and healthy competition for places,” said Carrick.

“Josh can do some really, really top things. I’ve seen it myself, and I know he can do that and looking forward to him doing that a little bit more often for us.”

After a dreadful 2-0 defeat at newly-promoted Hull on the opening weekend of the season, United bounced back to thrash Ipswich 5-2 thanks to a Bruno Fernandes hat-trick last time out.

Everton boss David Moyes conceded ‌he is left with a small squad after a disappointing transfer window in ⁠which key players departed ⁠and a deadline day medical fell through as they tried to sign American striker Folarin Balogun.

Moyes expressed frustration at his club’s close-season business, ⁠revealing they did not want to lose Senegal forward Iliman Ndiaye but were powerless when bigger teams like Manchester City look to sign their players.

“Disappointed we didn’t do more business ⁠and disappointed things didn’t go our way in the end. Sometimes in football you have to live with disappointment and we will move on,” Moyes told reporters on Friday.

“I know what I needed and I know what it’s like to build a squad for the Premier League, I know ‌the numbers you need. I’ve been around long enough to know that, but some things went against us and some things could have gone better.

“Ultimately, we didn’t want to lose a lot of the players, but for different reasons that had to happen.”

AS Monaco chief executive Thiago Scuro said Everton raised concerns over Balogun’s medical late on deadline day and that the US international pulled out because he was uncomfortable with the doubts ⁠raised by the Merseyside club over his health.

“It wasn’t anybody’s fault. ⁠It happens in football a lot,” Moyes said.

“The player had a problem in his medical and that was simply it. There’s no other story behind it.”

Everton’s Fans’ Forum also criticised the club’s planning and recruitment after the transfer ⁠window closed, saying supporters deserved answers after another window marked by late activity and a failed pursuit of key targets.

With a thin ⁠squad, Moyes said Everton’s academy players would have to step ⁠up but was unsure if they could fill the gaps.

“Are they ready to make the step up? I’m not sure about that. We will see how that goes, some of them might be pushed in,” Moyes said.

“They’re all ‌going to have to be able to muck in as we’ve got a real small squad now,” he added.

“It gives opportunities to some people who have not had them and sometimes ‌in ‌football you need to be given that chance so that you can show what you can do. Let’s see if some of them can do that.”

Manchester United were 1-0 winners in the last meeting of the sides, which came in a Premier League fixture at Hill Dickinson Stadium in February.

Benjamin Sesko scored the only goal after 71 minutes.

Everton won 1-0 in the Premier League fixture at Old Trafford last season – despite being reduced to ten men early on.

Idrissa Gueye was sent off in the 14th minute, while Kiernan Dewsbury-Hall came up with what would be the winner on the halfway mark.

The Opta supercomputer is giving Everton a 38.3 percent chance of winning, while offering United only a 33.3 percent chance of claiming the spoils.

This will be their 216th meeting with United winning 97 times and Everton 69.

The first meeting came in 1892 with Everton winning the English top flight encounter 6-0. The Toffees hit 10 against United that season as they completed the double with a 4-3 away win.

Jack Grealish is set to come straight into the matchday squad following his transfer deadline day loan from Manchester City.

Ainsley Maitland-Niles could also appear following the September 1 move for the ex-Arsenal defender. Christian Norgaard, another former Gunner, misses out with a knock.

Pickford; O’Brien, Tarkowski, Branthwaite, Mykolenko; Garner, Armstrong; Johnson, Dewsbury-Hall, Grealish; Barry

articles.title: Colombian government reports three killed in rebel attack on military post
articles.excerpt: Colombian authorities have said that at least three soldiers have been killed and several more injured after an attack on a military compound by an armed group that included drones used to drop explos...
articles.body_text:
Colombian authorities have said that at least three soldiers have been killed and several more injured after an attack on a military compound by an armed group that included drones used to drop explosives.

The Colombian army said on Saturday that the attack had been carried out by the rebel National Liberation Army (ELN) the night before in the municipality of Ocana, which is in the area bordering Venezuela. Two soldiers were killed in the clashes, along with a third who died after receiving medical attention. Four were injured.

“To the ELN I say with absolute clarity: for every police officer or soldier you kill, I will bring down on you the full weight and legitimate force of the State,” President Abelardo de la Espriella said in a statement on social media condemning the attack.

Authorities said that drones dropped explosives onto the compound in the department of Norte de Santander before fighting took place within the facility. The news service AFP reported that at least 20 drones loaded with explosives were utilised in the attack, citing an unnamed security official.

De la Espriella won office pledging to return Colombia to militarised confrontation with armed groups and criminal organisations that have jostled for influence across the country, despite concerns that it could lead to surging violence and possible rights abuses.

Deadly attacks by armed groups have continued to rattle the country since his inauguration.

The attack on Friday took place in the northeastern Catatumbo region, where the ELN is based and where the government has carried out military raids against armed groups.

De la Espriella has also promised closer ties with the United States, which has sought to expand its military involvement in the region under the so-called “Shield of the Americas” initiative.

US Secretary of State Marco Rubio is set to meet with de la Espriella, a former lawyer who previously represented leaders of paramilitaries, in the Caribbean city of Barranquilla next week.

articles.title: John Harbaugh and Jaxson Dart aim to pull the New York Giants out of the NFC East basement
articles.excerpt: Malik Nabers practiced in full for the 2nd-straught day, and John Harbaugh is bringing the hype to New York. Danny Parkins, Eric Mangini, and Geoff Schwartz ask if it’s time to buy Giants stock, and i...
articles.body_text:
Malik Nabers practiced in full for the 2nd-straught day, and John Harbaugh is bringing the hype to New York. Danny Parkins, Eric Mangini, and Geoff Schwartz ask if it’s time to buy Giants stock, and if Jalen Hurts and the Eagles will struggle this season. Plus, they ask if it’s possible that J.J. McCarthy isn’t on the Vikings by Week 1.

With John Harbaugh taking over as head coach and Jaxson Dart entering his first full year as the starter, the New York Giants aim to reset after multiple years of struggle.

But with championship-winning head coach Harbaugh stepping in to take the helm and second-year quarterback Dart taking over as the full-time leader under center, New York is aiming to prove that its structural reset is complete and that they can climb out of the NFC East basement.

The Giants suffered through a miserable 2025 campaign, finishing 4–13 and missing the postseason for the third consecutive year. New York showed flashes of an explosive future after rookie first-round pick Jaxson Dart took over in Week 4, bringing dynamic dual-threat playmaking and pulling off upset wins over the Los Angeles Chargers and Dallas Cowboys.

GIANTS' DRAFT PICK HAS INTENSE JAXSON DART MESSAGE: 'I’M READY TO DIE FOR YOU'

However, catastrophic defensive breakdowns and an inability to protect leads defined the season, as New York lost seven single-possession games and blew five double-digit leads. The mid-season firing of Brian Daboll signaled the end of the previous regime and set up a massive front-office overhaul entering the winter.

New York Giants quarterback Jaxson Dart throws a pass in the fourth quarter as the Giants beat the Dallas Cowboys 34-17 in East Rutherford on Jan. 4, 2026. (Kevin R. Wexler-NorthJersey.com / USA TODAY NETWORK via Imagn Images)

To fix the organizational culture, the biggest splash was the hiring cycle, luring longtime Ravens head coach John Harbaugh to East Rutherford, and then bringing in Matt Nagy as offensive coordinator to design a system around Dart.

In free agency and trade markets, the front office aggressively supplemented the roster with proven talent. They signed physical Baltimore tight end Isaiah Likely, while bolstering the defense with cornerback Paulson Adebo and safety Jevon Holland. On the subtraction side, New York parted ways with several depth pieces across the front seven and secondary while re-shaping the wide receiver room to prioritize fast, versatile weapons.

ZERO BS. JUST DAKICH. TAKE THE DON'T @ ME PODCAST ON THE ROAD. DOWNLOAD NOW!

John Harbaugh poses after a press conference announcing his hiring as the next New York Giants head coach at Quest Diagnostics Training Center in East Rutherford, New Jersey, on Jan. 20, 2026. (Ed Mulholland/Imagn Images)

There is reason for cautious, high-ceiling optimism when evaluating New York’s roster makeup. The offense relies heavily on Dart’s dual-threat versatility, backed by star wideout Malik Nabers on the perimeter (who is returning from injury) and the tight-end tandem of Isaiah Likely and Theo Johnson.

With an upgraded offensive line anchored by Andrew Thomas, the run game with Cam Skattebo (also returning from injury) and Tyrone Tracy Jr. should provide crucial balance. It will be up to the offensive line to find a way to make it work, though. They are ranked by PFF at 23rd in the league.

Defensively, the front seven boasts legitimate star power with edge rusher Brian Burns coming off an All-Pro-caliber campaign alongside Kayvon Thibodeaux and rookie pass-rush talent. With Adebo and Holland reinforcing a secondary that bled big plays last fall, the unit has the talent to transition from a liability into a formidable group. They will still need to win in the trenches, and their team is ranked 21st on the defensive line.

New York Giants quarterback Jaxson Dart (6) rushes the ball against the Chicago Bears during the second half at Soldier Field on Nov. 9, 2025 in Chicago, Illinois. (Mike Dinovo/Imagn Images)

I think under Harbaugh, you will see the Giants have an instant improvement. I’m not expecting them to win the division (I have the Cowboys). I do think they should get to seven wins, and potentially eight. Skattebo and Dart combined to provide some excitement, and if Nabers comes back healthy, this should be a fun team to watch. I still have a lot of questions about their defense, but the reality is that Harbaugh should show his impact in that aspect more than any other area. I’m probably not going to get heavily involved in the win total, but I do like the over.

Dart has a prop that I think he should hit. In 14 games, he threw 15 touchdowns with very few good options in most games. Now that he has more options, I think he hits over 19.5 touchdowns. Sure, Harbaugh seems to run the ball more often, but Nagy has been good for quarterbacks over the years. Give me over 19.5 touchdowns from Dart this season. I’d actually take this over 22.5 if there are alternate totals you can find.

For more sports betting information and plays, follow David on X/Twitter: @futureprez2024

articles.title: Jeff Foxworthy reveals how 'redneck' insult inspired decades of comedy
articles.excerpt:
Foxworthy was able to turn what should have been an insult into a "compliment" by turning it into a "badge of honor."

Jeff Foxworthy turned an insult into a compliment when someone criticized where h...
articles.body_text:
Foxworthy was able to turn what should have been an insult into a "compliment" by turning it into a "badge of honor."

Jeff Foxworthy turned an insult into a compliment when someone criticized where he came from.

During a recent interview with Fox News Digital, the 67-year-old actor and comedian discussed his new stand-up special, "The Joke's on Me," and recalled the time someone called him a "redneck," and how he turned what was meant to be an insult into a compliment.

He explained that "one of the nicest compliments" someone once gave him was commending his ability to turn what "was supposed to be an insult...into a badge of honor."

"I said, 'Well, that's cool, because when people get offended, they act like if you gave rednecks a billion dollars, they wouldn't be rednecks,'" he said. "I said they would still be rednecks. They would just have bigger boats, bigger truck. I mean, more things to shoot at. They're happy with who they are. And I've always got asked, ‘How do you come up with that?’ And I'm like. There's no research going on. It's my family and my friend group that trust me."

Foxworthy explained how he turned an insult into a joke for his stand-up routine. (Paras Griffin/Getty Images)

DAVE CHAPPELLE SAYS HE’S CONSIDERING REVISITING ‘CHAPPELLE’S SHOW’ DECADES AFTER WALKING AWAY

Foxworthy first began telling jokes about rednecks in the late '80s, and found them to be extremely successful, so he continued telling them, even closing his 1990 special with one.

He explained that "they were easy to remember" and said they would always "get a laugh." After telling the jokes on stage for a while, he "thought, well people are tired of this," and stopped telling them, adding, "The last time I did them onstage was during the Blue Collar Comedy Tour" in 2003.

WATCH: Foxworthy explained how he turned an insult into a joke for his stand-up.

After more than 20 years of staying away from the jokes, Foxworthy felt like it was time to bring them back. He recalled telling the crowd, "I hadn't done these in 20 years, but I'm thinking about for this special, bringing them back."

"I said that because when I said that if you've ever peed in the pool, the entire audience went, 'You might be a redneck.' And I went, 'Oh, wow, this stuck to people's bones, you know?'" he said. "And I say, well, what if I did some to close, if that was my first special, and all these years later, this is my last. It kind of seemed like a nice little way to put a bow on it."

Foxworthy brought jokes about rednecks back into his act after realizing they still resonated with his audience. (Gary Gershoff/Getty Images)

He then went back and looked at all the redneck jokes he had written over the years, "and pulled out a bunch of them" to try at his next gig at a comedy club.

"It was like, I never stopped doing them," he said. "It was like going back 35 years, which was really cool for me. It's like one of your babies. You bring it back out and people go, 'Oh, we still love it.'"

WATCH: Jeff Foxworthy explains why he stopped telling 'redneck' jokes

Foxworthy's latest comedy special, "The Joke's on Me" began streaming on Fox Nation in June. Unlike other comedy specials, this one gives fans a behind-the-scenes look at the joke writing process that goes into creating a special.

The comedian told Fox News Digital he was inspired to create the unique special after watching a documentary about the Beatles and realizing that "seeing the process didn't take anything away from the finished product," but rather made it better "because you saw the struggle that went into creating that."

LIKE WHAT YOU'RE READING? CLICK HERE FOR MORE ENTERTAINMENT NEWS

Foxworthy came up with the idea for his new special after watching a documentary about the Beatles. (Getty Images)

GET ENTERTAINMENT SCOOP DELIVERED RIGHT TO YOUR EMAIL BY CLICKING HERE

When Fox Nation approached him with the offer to do a stand-up special, he pitched them the behind-the-scenes idea.

"I said, 'But if you're willing to try something different, if you will show me note cards in hand, going into a club on a Tuesday night or a Wednesday night and just throwing these thoughts out.' Because one of the things that still fascinates me after over 40 years about stand-up is I still don't know what people are gonna laugh at," he said.

He added: "You would think after 40 years, I would know. Now I'll go in there with an idea, 'Oh, this is really funny.' And then nobody laughs. Or I'll have a card where I think this is so stupid, I'm embarrassed to say it, and you throw it out there and everybody's beaten the tables laughing. And you're like, really? And so I wanted to show that. And Fox Nation was the first place that ever said, 'Okay, we'll do it.'"

Foxworthy has hinted that this could be his last stand-up special, but assures fans that doesn't mean he will never perform on a stage again.

PUT YOUR ENTERTAINMENT KNOWLEDGE TO THE TEST AND SEE HOW YOU SCORE

Foxworthy hinted this may be his last stand-up special. (Paras Griffin/Getty Images for Beloved Benefit)

He told Fox News Digital that he has reached a point in his life where the time he would spend on the road, he would rather spend with his grandkids or on his tractor.

WATCH: Jeff Foxworthy clears up his comments about retiring from stand-up

"I've been on the road nonstop," he added. "I laugh at my music friends when they say they're on tour. I said, 'Well, tour implies it stops. At some point,' I said, 'I've been on tour since 1984.' It just never stopped. I still love stand-up. I just don't know that I'm willing. And to be honest, I'm not sure I can do anything any better than this, which just feels like a good place to stop."

Foxworthy's Fox Nation special, titled "The Joke's On Me," is available to watch now.

Lori A. Bashian is an entertainment news writer at Fox News Digital.

articles.title: Baking legend’s 1960s home hits market with original details and a very unusual kitchen
articles.excerpt: Kate Freebairn, Australia-based author of "Easy Sourdough on Any Schedule," reveals how home bakers can prepare a loaf around family and job commitments with only brief periods spent handling the doug...
articles.body_text:
Kate Freebairn, Australia-based author of "Easy Sourdough on Any Schedule," reveals how home bakers can prepare a loaf around family and job commitments with only brief periods spent handling the dough.

The home of a nationally famous baker who died last year at the age of 106 is up for sale for the first time, and the 1968 house is being described as a "time capsule" for its original fixtures and custom kitchen that have been meticulously maintained for more than half a century.

Marjorie Johnson, of Robbinsdale, Minn., got hooked on competitive baking when, at age 55, she entered four baked items in the 1974 Minnesota State Fair, winning three ribbons.

FROM FONDUE TO CASSEROLES: CLASSIC 1960S FOODS THAT DEFINED A GENERATION

She would go on to win more than 3,000 state and county fair ribbons — so many that she lost count — and became a national television personality known as the "Blue Ribbon Baker," with regular appearances on "The Tonight Show with Jay Leno" and other national talk shows.

Rosie O’Donnell wrote the foreword to her cookbook, "The Road to Blue Ribbon Baking: With Marjorie." The Minnesota State Fair introduced the new Marjorie Johnson Honey Bee Award this year to recognize the blue-ribbon baker in the honey sweet rolls category.

The Robbinsdale, Minn. home of famed "Blue Ribbon Baker" Marjorie Johnson has hit the market for the first time since it was built in 1968. (Paul Drinkwater/NBC/NBCU Photo Bank)

Johnson "personally picked out everything" in the 5,100-square-foot lakefront home where she perfected countless recipes and raised a family with husband Leroy "Lee" Johnson, the couple’s daughter Marilee Wheaton told The Minnesota Star Tribune.

"This was my mom’s dream house," daughter Marleen Stromme told the publication. "She spent countless hours going through and making sure everything was just how she wanted."

Standing at about 4 feet, 9 inches tall, Johnson designed the countertops and a low desk in the kitchen to accommodate her stature.

The powder-blue kitchen has extra freezers and is "filled with cabinets for every necessary utensil and baking instrument," the Star Tribune reported.

Other features of the two-story house include six bedrooms, four bathrooms and built-ins throughout, as well as an indoor pool in the basement and 70 feet of shoreline on Crystal Lake, FOX 9 Minneapolis-St. Paul reported.

Johnson’s son, Steve, told the Star Tribune his mother swam in the pool every day until she turned 80.

Johnson’s baking success eventually took her from the Minnesota State Fair to national television, including regular appearances on "The Tonight Show with Jay Leno." (Kevin Winter/Tonight Show/Getty Images for The Tonight Show)

There’s also a second kitchen and family room, a two-car garage and a three-season room with a view of the lake.

Shag carpet, floral wallpaper, pink bathroom tile and a built-in record player are among the vintage touches Johnson carefully preserved that give the house a nostalgic feel.

CLICK HERE TO SIGN UP FOR OUR LIFESTYLE NEWSLETTER

"The chrome just shines, and there are no cracks in the tile," the home’s listing agent, Jeanne LeVasseur of Keller Williams Realty, told FOX 9. "All of the fixtures, all of them still work, so it’s kind of unheard of. I mean people are like, 'I definitely had to come and see the house because of her.' She’s a legacy."

Johnson was known for her energy and upbeat personality.

Johnson’s celebrity extended beyond the fairgrounds, with Rosie O’Donnell writing the foreword to her cookbook, "The Road to Blue Ribbon Baking: With Marjorie." (Ida Mae Astute/Disney General Entertainment Content via Getty Images)

"Everybody who wants to live and feel good, and not die in their 60s and 70s and 80s, they have to think positive," she told the Star Tribune. "What I do, is I wake up in the morning and say to myself, ‘Today is going to be a wonderful day.’ And at the end of the day, it will be a wonderful day."

The home is listed for $665,000. FOX 9 reported the family has already received several offers and hopes to make a decision on a new owner soon.

TEST YOURSELF WITH OUR LATEST LIFESTYLE QUIZ

"It is a blue-ribbon house and it is absolutely my mom's dream house," Wheaton told the station. "The whole house was filled with love. It was filled with smells of all that baking."

"I feel like there is someone out there that is going to love it as much as my mom loved it," she added.

Teresa Mull is a freelance writer with the Lifestyle team at Fox News Digital.

articles.title: Brooke Hogan threatens to expose family receipts in 'final warning'
articles.excerpt:
HGTV "Rock the Block" contestant Brooke Hogan tells Fox News Digital about her grief and healing journey after her father’s death.

Brooke Hogan is warning her family that she has receipts, and she's ...
articles.body_text:
HGTV "Rock the Block" contestant Brooke Hogan tells Fox News Digital about her grief and healing journey after her father’s death.

Brooke Hogan is warning her family that she has receipts, and she's prepared to use them.

The 38-year-old daughter of late wrestling legend  fired back after her mother, Linda Hogan, publicly lamented their yearslong estrangement and accused Brooke of tossing her family aside "like trash."

"This 👌 close to breaking out some screenshots – which are ONE of the many reasons WHY," Brooke wrote over a screenshot of her mother's Facebook post from August 30 shared to her Instagram Story.

BROOKE HOGAN SAYS ‘I COULD HAVE SAVED YOU’ IN HAUNTING REGRET AFTER HULK HOGAN’S DEATH

Brooke Hogan threatened to bring out the "receipts" as her bitter family feud with mother Linda Hogan erupted again. (Brooke Hogan Oleksy/Instagram )

"I don't take CONSTANTLY dragging my name through the mud lightly," she continued.

"The selective amnesia isn't gonna work."

Brooke ended the message with two words: "Final warning."

The latest flare-up came after Linda shared old family photos on Facebook while expressing her frustration over her fractured relationship with her daughter.

"I posted these wonderful photos of Brooke my daughter with me and my ex-husband her father and my mom and dad and really .. the whole family ! Brooke is loved," Linda wrote.

"We feel hurt every day that she just tosses us aside .... like trash," she continued. "I want to make sure she remembers how it really was .. and can really see how much she was adored and loved."

Brooke's response suggested she remembers their family history differently and is prepared to make private communications public if the criticism continues.

The mother and daughter's latest exchange is another chapter in a family fracture that has played out publicly for years.

PUT YOUR ENTERTAINMENT KNOWLEDGE TO THE TEST AND SEE HOW YOU SCORE

Brooke Hogan is seen with her brother, Nick Hogan, and parents Hulk Hogan and Linda Hogan. (Michael Loccisano/FilmMagic)

Brooke first became famous alongside her parents, Hulk and Linda, and younger brother, Nick Hogan, on the VH1 reality series "Hogan Knows Best," which premiered in 2005.

The show followed the wrestling superstar and his family while also documenting Brooke's budding music career and her father's protective approach to his teenage daughter.

GET ENTERTAINMENT SCOOP DELIVERED RIGHT TO YOUR EMAIL BY CLICKING HERE

The family dynamic changed dramatically after Linda filed for divorce from Hulk in 2007 following more than two decades of marriage. Their divorce was finalized in 2009.

Years later, Brooke became estranged from both parents, but she has made clear that her reasons for cutting contact with her mother were separate from the issues she had with her father.

Brooke addressed the family rift directly in a lengthy Instagram statement on March 27, 2025, insisting she had not chosen one parent over the other.

"No contact with my mom has nothing to do with my dad, and no contact with my father has nothing to do with my mother," Brooke wrote. "I have completely separate reasons for going no contact with each of my parents."

HAYDEN PANETTIERE AND THE CHILD STARS WHOSE RELATIONSHIPS WITH THEIR MOMAGERS TURNED COMPLICATED

In the same statement, Brooke made serious allegations about her childhood and family relationships.

"I have been EXTREMELY verbally and mentally abused since childhood," she alleged. "Sadly, it would frequently turn physical. And sometimes it's not by the person you would assume, abuse comes in all shapes and sizes."

Brooke did not identify a specific person in that portion of her statement.

The Hogan family is seen at the 2004 Radio Music Awards in Las Vegas in October 2004. (Frank Micelotta/Getty Images)

She also claimed she had been put in the position of publicly defending behavior within her family before eventually questioning what she had been told.

"I've been asked to defend poor behavior to the public and have done so out of love. Only to find I was misinformed, manipulated, and lied to," she wrote.

"I longed for a normal family, but it never came to fruition. I've repeatedly held my hand out to help them, only to have them pull me into the darkness with them."

She continued, "I've set boundaries that were not respected, which turned into a 'no contact' situation."

Her comments came after Linda publicly discussed the family's troubles in March 2025, reigniting attention around their strained relationship.

The conflict marked a dramatic departure from the image viewers were introduced to two decades earlier on "Hogan Knows Best."

Brooke was a teenager when the series premiered, with the show following her budding music career, dating life and her father's famously protective parenting.

WWE LEGEND HULK HOGAN'S DEATH REPORT RELEASED

Brooke previously told Fox News Digital that despite her strained relationship with her father, she loved him. (Acey Harper/Getty Images)

In the years that followed, the family relationships viewers once watched on television became increasingly strained, with some of those disputes eventually playing out in public.

Her relationship with her father received renewed attention following his death on July 24, 2025.

Hulk, born Terry Bollea, died at age 71 after being hospitalized for cardiac arrest.

Hulk was survived by Brooke and Nick, whom he shared with Linda, as well as his wife, Sky Daily.

Despite being estranged from her father when he died, Brooke made clear in an April interview with Fox News Digital that her love for him had never disappeared.

"I’m honest with him now, and I talk to him all the time, even if that seems like I’m a cuckoo bird," she told Fox News Digital. "If he showed up today, I would just be like, ‘I love you so much, and I wish you would have just let me in.’"

Brooke also offered rare insight into why their relationship had become strained before his death.

Brooke said that she wanted to "save" her father before his death. (John Parra/WireImage)

"[It's] tough because, obviously, my dad and I weren't really speaking prior to his death — not because I didn't love him… it's that he had become a little bit calloused in the direction he was going in his life and the people he was surrounding himself with," she said.

LIKE WHAT YOU'RE READING? CLICK HERE FOR MORE ENTERTAINMENT NEWS

"I am the daughter that wanted to save him. And it's kind of like, you can try to save somebody and if they don't want to be saved… it's a tough position to be in."

Her comments to Fox News Digital echoed what Brooke had emphasized in her March 2025 statement: distancing herself from her father did not mean she had sided with her mother, or vice versa.

Fox News Digital's Stephanie Giang-Paunon contributed to this report.

Danielle Minnetian is an Entertainment Production Assistant for Fox News Digital covering celebrity news, entertainment trends and pop culture.
